title: How Hanukkah Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain Hanukkah on the last day of the holiday: the Maccabean revolt against Seleucid king Antiochus IV and the 167 BC Jewish rebellion led by Mattathias and his son Judah Maccabee, the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem around 164 BC, the one-night oil miracle lasting eight nights, and how it is observed (menorah and shamash, candle blessings, dreidel and gelt, fried foods like latkes and sufganiyot). They contrast it with Christmas, mention the "Hanukkah Harry" sketch, and close with a listener mail about a medieval dinner show job.

segments.title: Opening banter and Hanukkah Harry
segments.summary: Hosts note the last day of Hanukkah and explain they are covering it after Christmas-themed episode. They joke about 'Hanukkah Harry,' a SNL-style sketch portraying a Hanukkah version of Santa who delivers socks and slacks.

segments.title: Antiochus IV and the Maccabean revolt
segments.summary: Antiochus IV persecutes Jews in Jerusalem, forcing Greek idol worship. Mattathias and his five sons, the Hasmoneans, refuse and start the rebellion in 167 BC; Judah, called Judah the Hammer (Maccabee), leads it.

segments.title: Rededication of the Temple and the oil miracle
segments.summary: Around 165 BC the rebels retake the Temple in Jerusalem on the 25th of Kislev and rededicate it. A single night's supply of oil lasts eight nights, the origin of the eight-night holiday.

segments.title: Hanukkah versus Christmas and Americanization
segments.summary: Hosts state Hanukkah is not Jewish Christmas, a festival of lights commemorating a miracle, and note how American culture absorbs holidays, comparing it to Mexico and Canada as joking body parts.

segments.title: Menorah, candle lighting and blessings
segments.summary: Candles are placed right to left but lit left to right, with the shamash used to light the others. Candles burn at least half an hour after dark, and on Shabbat they are lit before sundown. Chuck reads the three blessings in Hebrew and Josh translates them.

segments.title: Dreidel and gelt
segments.summary: The dreidel has four Hebrew letters (nun, gimel, hey, shin) standing for a great miracle happened there, and Yiddish equivalents for outcomes. Players bet gelt on the spin, which the hosts debate as gambling. The game's history as cover for secret Torah study is told.

segments.title: Hanukkah foods: latkes and sufganiyot
segments.summary: Foods are fried in oil to honor the oil miracle, including potato pancakes (latkes) and jelly donuts (sufganiyot) dusted with powdered sugar.

segments.title: Listener mail: Medieval Times job
segments.summary: Gerald writes about working as the Master of Ceremonies at a Medieval Times-style dinner show, where the script contained inaccurate history. The hosts respond and ask listeners about their worst jobs.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wish a happy holiday to listeners of all faiths and promote the website search for more on Hanukkah.
